title: Toast wraps at half the viewport width on phones: tall broken pill over content
detail: Any toast longer than ~25 characters on iPhone wraps into a 201px-wide, 3-line 'pill' (radius pill on a tall box) sitting over the page content above the tab bar. Reproduced with KOS.ui.toast('You already had 44 badge tiers — they are on the Badge Wall.') at 402x874: rect x=100.5 w=201 h=78.5. Same on every width: the toast can never be wider than half the viewport.
evidence: shots/shell/toast-iphone.png; eval rect [100.5,735.5,201,78.5]; css/components.css:389-405 (#toast: position fixed; inset-inline-start:50%; translate(-50%) with shrink-to-fit width)
fix: Give the toast an explicit fit-content width independent of its left offset: e.g. inset-inline:0; margin-inline:auto; inline-size:fit-content; max-inline-size:min(var(--toast-max), calc(100% - var(--sp-32))); transform only on Y. Use a rounded-rect radius (r-16) when it wraps, or keep pill only for one line.
rootCause: A fixed element with left:50% gets an available width of (viewport - 50%) for shrink-to-fit sizing, so text wraps at 50% of the viewport before the max-inline-size ever applies.
devices: iPhone (all phones); also iPad/Mac for long toasts (wraps at 410/735px)

title: Nothing redraws the open page when the day changes: header clock says Mon 2 Nov, Home still says Sunday 1 November / Good evening
detail: Left open across midnight (the user's installed iPad app is), the header clock ticks to the new date but the current view is never redrawn, so Home keeps yesterday's date line, greeting, Today list and daily goal until something else triggers a redraw. Observed at 00:00: header 'Mon 2 Nov', hero 'SUNDAY 1 NOVEMBER · Good evening', while the Week's plan card in the same page (drawn later) already read 'w/c 2 Nov'. A manual KOS.rerender() then showed 'Monday 2 November · Working late'.
evidence: shots/shell/bell-mac.png (clock 00:00 Mon 2 Nov vs hero Sunday 1 November); js/main.js:86-97 (only the clock ticks every 20 s); js/main.js:199-204 (30-min interval refreshes HUD and rail counters but never the view); hub.js:623 reads new Date() only when drawn
fix: In tickClock, remember the date string; when it changes (and on visibilitychange after a day boundary) call KOS.rerender() if no dialog/ink/Focus is busy (the rerender already waits on KOS.inkUI.busy).
rootCause: Day-dependent views read new Date() only at draw time and the shell has no day-rollover redraw.
devices: all; most visible on the installed iPad app

title: Phone search chips file Goals under 'Collection' and Reports/Files under a fake 'Pages' section
detail: Searching 'goal' on iPhone shows chips 'All 11 · Study 5 · Collection 6' where the six 'Collection' results are all Goals. Goals has been a Productivity page since 27a (CLAUDE.md invariant 27). Reports and Files groups have no mapping and fall back to a 'Pages' chip, although neither is a pages result (Reports lives under Home, Files under Archive).
evidence: shots/shell/search-iphone-q.png; js/modules/hub.js:3592-3593 (SEARCH_SECTION: goals: "Collection"; reports/files absent → "Pages" at :3598)
fix: goals → Productivity, planner → Collection (Wishlist), reports → Home, files → Archive; derive the section from the same table the rail uses (KOS.sectionLanding / the rail's section ids) so a new domain cannot silently fall to 'Pages'.
rootCause: Hard-coded section table not updated when Goals moved to Productivity and when Reports/Files search domains were added.

title: Global search cannot find app pages or features (typing 'money', 'goals', 'help', 'settings' finds no page)
detail: Search covers records (spec, notes, reminders, assignments, calendar, wishlist, goals, cards, media, reports, files) but no navigation entries. 'money' returns six specification leaves (Code 1.7, 5.3, CS data types…) and nothing that opens Money; the same for 'routines', 'help', 'exams', 'badges', 'connections', 'storage'. For a one-connected-OS app with ~40 pages behind 7 rail sections and the phone's 5 tabs, a page jump is the fastest route. Also missing domains: Exams hub assessments, Routines/habits, Money (payee search, if privacy allows), Help entries, achievements. A Goals result opens the Goals list (KOS.show('goals')), not the goal itself, and prints the raw status ('completed', 'active').
evidence: shots/shell/search-mac-money.png; shots/shell/search-iphone-q.png; js/core/search.js:291-307 (domain list), :194-199 (goal result opens 'goals', sub = g.status)
fix: Add a synchronous 'Pages' domain built from the rail/section tables (title + aliases like 'budget'→Money, 'badges'→Achievements, 'help'), ranked first on an exact page-name hit; add assessments and routines domains; open a goal at #/goals/<id> and print a human status.
rootCause: search.js only has record domains; the navigation map lives in the rail/mobile-shell and is not exposed to search.

title: Global Backspace = Back fires even when a page handled the key: Backspace on a Money row opens 'Delete this entry?' AND navigates to the previous page underneath
detail: js/main.js binds Backspace (outside text fields) to KOS.back() on document and never checks e.defaultPrevented. Money's transaction list uses Delete/Backspace on a focused row to delete it (money.js:610) and calls preventDefault, but the document listener still runs: reproduced on #/money/transactions → focus a row → Backspace: the confirm dialog opens while the route has already changed to #/home behind it; cancelling leaves the user on Home, having lost their place. Any future in-page Backspace handler (ink lasso selection, lists, the editor's rows, Mind's list at mindui.js:154 which is inside a textarea so is safe) collides the same way. Backspace-as-Back is also surprising on its own: a stray Backspace with focus on any button (after clicking a card, closing a menu) leaves the page; browsers removed this shortcut for that reason.
evidence: shots/shell/backspace-money-dialog-over-home.png; eval result {hash:'#/home', dialog:'Delete this entry? QA coffee, −£4.50…'}; js/main.js:20-28; js/modules/money.js:610
fix: In main.js return early when e.defaultPrevented, when a dialog is open, or when the target is inside [role=listbox]/[data-keys]; better, drop bare Backspace and keep Alt+←/→ (and ⌘[ / ⌘] on the Mac). Register the listener in the bubble phase after page handlers (it already is) and respect defaultPrevented.
rootCause: The shell's history shortcut ignores defaultPrevented and treats any non-text target as free to navigate.

title: Governor ⋯ menu is cut off behind the Stage (only half of its first row shows)
detail: On #/governor, ⋯ in the page header opens a 280x100 (mac) / 280x136 (iPad) popover whose 'HP preview' row is cut in half and whose 'Data: Mine/Empty/Sample' row is completely hidden behind the Stage card below. Same at 1470x832, 1180x820 and 820x1180.
evidence: shots/shell/gov-menu-mac.png, shots/shell/gov-menu-ipad.png, shots/shell/gov-menu-ipadl.png; popover rect mac {x:1165,y:164,w:280,h:100}; css/components.css:35 (.k-pagehead[data-state~=has-art] {position:relative; isolation:isolate}); css/views/governor.css:31 (.k-gv-stage {position:relative; isolation:isolate}) and :65 (.k-gv-tools-pop z-index var(--z-menu)); js/modules/governor-ui.js:420-439 (an inline <details> popover)
fix: Use the shared KOS.ui.menu (it portals the panel to <body>, js/core/ui.js ~813) instead of a hand-made <details>; or give the painted page header z-index:var(--z-sticky) so its stacking context sits above the following content. Audit any other in-header inline popover after the 34e painted headers.
rootCause: 34e made painted page headers an isolated stacking context; the z-index of the popover now only counts inside the header, and the Stage that follows (also isolated, later in DOM) paints over it. The Governor menu is a one-off <details> rather than the portalled KOS.ui.menu.

title: Phone '⋯ tools' and section-switch sheets stay open when the window grows past 700px, showing a phone sheet as a desktop modal
detail: Open #/governor at 402px, tap ⋯ (Status tools), then widen to 1470: the 'Status' sheet stays open centred on the desktop page, holding the moved Live/Full/Off and Mine/Empty/Sample segments, while the desktop header's own ⋯ menu is now empty of them. Happens with iPad Split View / Slide Over resizing and any desktop window resize. syncShell() closes the More and Search overlays when leaving phone width but not activeToolsOverlay or activeSectionOverlay.
evidence: shots/shell/phone-sheet-left-open-at-mac.png; js/modules/mobile-shell.js:584-589 (only activeMoreOverlay/activeSearchOverlay are closed), :516-539 (openTools moves the nodes out of the page)
fix: In syncShell when !phone.matches also close activeToolsOverlay and activeSectionOverlay (their onClose already puts the nodes back).
rootCause: The phone→wide cleanup list in syncShell was not extended when the tools and section sheets were added.
devices: iPad Split View/Slide Over, Mac window resize

title: Phone ⋯ tools sheet drops the group labels: Governor's sheet shows bare 'Live Full Off' and 'Mine Empty Sample' with no idea what they control
detail: Only the [data-phone-more] segment nodes are moved into the sheet; their sibling labels ('HP preview', 'Data') stay behind in the hidden desktop popover. On iPhone the 'Status' sheet is two unlabelled segmented rows. These are also review/test aids (the summary's own label is 'Test controls': HP preview and an Empty/Sample account switch) exposed in the production header of a page the user visits daily.
evidence: shots/shell/gov-menu-iphone.png; js/modules/governor-ui.js:423-430 (labels are spans outside the data-phone-more nodes); js/modules/mobile-shell.js:516-520
fix: Mark the label+segment pair (a wrapper) as data-phone-more, or let openTools read each node's aria-label as a visible caption. Consider moving the test controls to Archive › developer settings or hiding them behind a setting.
rootCause: openTools moves nodes individually and has no notion of a caption.

title: iPhone bottom tab bar lost its labels: five bare kanji (灯 学 整 蒐 余) with no Home/Study/Productivity/Collection/More text
detail: On iPhone the tab bar shows only the 28px kanji tiles; the English labels are clipped to a 1x1 rect. Design 15a and layout.css's own phone block intend visible labels ('the tree states' compact-rail rules must not clip the tab labels on a phone'). A user who does not read kanji cannot tell 整 from 蒐; the profile/More sheet is the only place the names appear. Screen readers still get the names (sr-only clip), so this is visual only.
evidence: shots/shell/seed-home-iphone.png, shots/shell/more-iphone.png (bar at y=818-874); eval: label rect {w:1,h:1}, clip rect(0px,0px,0px,0px), #cols has no data-rail and data-tree=none on a phone; css/layout.css:377 (inside @media max-width:1080px: #cols:not([data-rail="full"]) .k-rail-label {position:absolute; clip:rect(0 0 0 0)} — specificity 1,2,0) beats css/layout.css:433 (.k-rail-label {position:static…} — 0,1,0) and :431 only covers data-rail=compact / tree open|closed
fix: In the ≤700 block add the same reset for the 1080 tier's selector: '#cols:not([data-rail="full"]) .k-rail-label, #cols:not([data-rail="full"]) .k-rail-count { position: static; inline-size:auto; block-size:auto; clip:auto; overflow:visible }' (or scope the 1080 rule with min-width:701px). Add a smoke/visual assertion that a phone tab label has width > 20px.
rootCause: Regression from 4c29a2f (feat(ipad), 22 Oct): the iPad tier's ID-scoped label-hiding rule also matches at phone width and out-specifies the phone's class-level reset.

title: In-app Help & Guide is missing most features released since mid-October (Money, Goals, Reports, Exams hub, Code, Japanese, Mind, Creatives, Achievements, Connections, the Assistant, the shop/Stage)
detail: js/modules/help.js SECTIONS (8 sections, 79 entries) was last touched 26 Oct and has NO entry at all for: (1) Money — the six views, budgets and pace, recurring bills/income/subscriptions and trials, pots, CSV, Hide amounts, the Wishlist purchase handoff (0 mentions of 'Money'); (2) Goals — the Goals page, types, repeating goals, exam goals, the Home switch (the only mention is the outdated 'Planner' entry); (3) Reports — week/month/term/year, the story, share card, Kurenai's words; (4) the Exams & Deadlines hub — assessments, scopes, readiness, the planner, Exam Season, Exam Room, Paper library, Companion, predicted papers (Help only has the old 'Exams & Papers' tracker, 'Log every exam… and a reviewed checkbox'); (5) Code (only 'Rider projects and GitHub'; nothing on the desk, lessons, runners, Daily 20, katas, capstones); (6) Japanese; (7) Mind; (8) Creatives; (9) Achievements / the Badge Wall / titles / showcase; (10) the Governor's Seat as the Stage, Edit seat, Gold Shop items and Try on, Wardrobe, Avatar & profile, Follow the system, painted pictures and 'Your own picture' unlocks; (11) Archive › Connections (Google Calendar, Google Tasks, Todoist); (12) the Kurenai Assistant itself (chat, approval cards, scheduled messages, memory, Kurenai's states/Hide); (13) closed-app notifications ('When the app is closed', Send a test), notification filters and quiet hours as settings; (14) writing by hand beyond Archive › Pen and ink (the Handwritten tab, Side by side, Clip to page, answer pads, the Working pane, palette/ruler, Mark with Kurenai, ink sync and clashes); (15) FSRS settings (target retention, exam-day target, the optimiser). The Help nav and its on-page search therefore return nothing for 'money', 'goal', 'badge', 'japanese', 'report'.
evidence: shots/shell/help-mac.png, shots/shell/help-iphone.png; grep counts in js/modules/help.js: Money 0, Mind 0, Creatives 0, Achievement 0, Badge 0, Connections 0, Todoist 0, Japanese 0, Reports 0, Assistant 0; git log -1 js/modules/help.js = 26 Oct 2026
fix: Add sections: Money & Goals, Reports, Exams & Deadlines (replace 'Exams & Papers'), Study spaces (Code, Japanese, Mind, Creatives), Achievements, The Governor's Seat & shop, Assistant, Connections, Notifications (move out of Collection), Writing by hand; give each a 'Open …' relation like the others. Add a smoke check that every rail destination / KOS.views id with a page header has at least one Help entry.
rootCause: Help is a hand-kept array with no test tying it to the set of views, so each release added pages without entries.

title: Help & Guide entries that are now wrong
detail: Out of date or false: 'Overview' (Home has no 'completion ring' or 'subject cards'; it is Up next/Today/Upcoming/Study hours/report/plan/routines); 'Subjects (rail)' (the rail has no subjects — sections only; subjects are pills in two groups); 'Search (topbar)' ('every spec point and flashcard across all three subjects' — it searches 11 domains and 7+ subjects); 'Back / Forward' ('The ‹ › buttons' — there are none: #nav-back/#nav-fwd do not exist in index.html, main.js:16-19 binds to null; it also omits that bare Backspace navigates back); 'Planner' ('holds Budget Planner and Goals under one secondary tab bar' — Goals is a Productivity page, the Planner is the Wishlist, the budget is Money); 'Notifications' is filed under 'The Collection Matrix' and mentions 'a Budget Planner item'; 'Autosave' ('the AUTOSAVE dot pulses' — no #save-dot exists in index.html); 'XP & level' ('The HUD in the topbar shows avatar, level, gold, HP and XP… click it' — the HUD is the rail foot / More sheet, not the topbar); 'Today's directives' (no such Home list; its link opens Routines); 'Countdowns' ('The rail merges…' — there is no countdown rail); 'Exams & Papers' (a 'reviewed checkbox' tracker; now the Exams hub); 'Sample data' (only calendar SAMPLE events, while the empty account also shows SAMPLE mock/deadline assessments, see empty-home shots). The 'Data & housekeeping' section shows a '·' where every other section has a kanji glyph. docs/GUIDE.md §5 'What is still on the way' still lists Creatives, Mind, the art pass and shop outfits, all released; GUIDE says Money 'stays on your device' although transactions replicate to kos_money.
evidence: shots/shell/help-mac.png ('·' before Data & housekeeping, 'Alt ← / →' shortcut only); js/modules/help.js lines 2-5, 40, 57, 62, 78-79 and the 'Autosave' entry; index.html (no nav-back, nav-fwd, save-dot); js/main.js:15-19; docs/GUIDE.md:158 and :418-431
fix: Rewrite those entries against the current app; give 'Data & housekeeping' a glyph; add Backspace (or remove the shortcut, see the Backspace finding) to Useful shortcuts; refresh GUIDE.md §5 and the Money sentence.
rootCause: Docs not updated with releases; no test.

title: Help on iPhone: section chips wrap into a ragged left-aligned cloud
detail: At 402px the eight section chips wrap one or two per line with uneven widths and a large empty right side (e.g. 'The Behavioural Governor 7' alone on a row, 'Data & housekeeping' alone), pushing the article below the fold. Other pages use a horizontal KOS.ui.scroller for this.
evidence: shots/shell/help-iphone.png
fix: Use the shared scroller (one line, horizontally scrollable, declared overflow) or the phone title bar's section switch for the eight sections.
rootCause: help.css nav reflows as flex-wrap at phone width.

title: document.title never changes: every page, history entry and app-switcher card reads "Kurenai OS — Study Atelier"
detail: Only Focus writes document.title (the countdown). Navigating to Money, Goals, a topic, Help etc. leaves the same title, so the browser history menu, Back long-press list, Safari tabs, the Mac window title and screen-reader page announcements cannot tell pages apart (WCAG 2.4.2 Page Titled). The brand elsewhere is "Kurenai".
evidence: eval after navigating to #/calendar: title "Kurenai OS — Study Atelier"; grep document.title → only js/modules/focus.js:1072,1494
fix: In router.js after a successful show, set document.title = "<page h1 or section label> · Kurenai" (Focus keeps prefixing its countdown).
rootCause: The router owns the URL but not the title.

title: Unknown or stale deep links fall back silently (to Home, or to a list) with no message
detail: #/nonsense/xyz and #/topic/cs/9.9.9 replace to #/home with nothing said; #/goals/doesnotexist shows the Goals list with the bad id still in the URL. A link from an old notification, report or a deleted goal therefore looks like the app ignored the tap.
evidence: eval: invalid → #/home, badTopic → #/home, badGoal → stays #/goals/doesnotexist showing the list
fix: When the router replaces an invalid route, toast "That page is no longer here" (and for a missing record, "That goal was deleted") and normalise the URL.
rootCause: invariant 65 replaces invalid routes with Home but nothing tells the user.

title: Collapsed rail (Mac, iPad portrait) is kanji-only with no tooltip and drops the due-count badge
detail: Collapsing the rail on the Mac (and the default iPad-portrait rail) shows 灯 学 整 蒐 守 助 蔵 with no title/tooltip on hover, so a mouse user cannot discover what 整 or 蔵 is without expanding; the Study due count (373) is clipped away with the label, so the at-a-glance signal disappears. The rail toggle itself is a 24px circle overlapping the rail edge (24x24 also on the touch iPad by design, below the 44px coarse target).
evidence: shots/shell/rail-collapsed-mac.png; shots/shell/empty-home-ipad.png; eval: rail items have no title attribute; toggle rect 24x24 at (59,76); css/layout.css:213-235, :377
fix: Give each rail item title=<label> (or a CSS tooltip on :hover/:focus-visible when compact); show the count as a small dot/number on the tile when compact; give the toggle a 44px invisible hit area on coarse pointers (padding + negative margin) while drawing the 24px circle.
rootCause: The compact rail hides label and count together via the same sr-only clip.

title: Search result sub-lines print raw data: 'Due 2026-10-28', goal status 'completed'/'active'
detail: Reminder results read 'Reminder 2 · Due 2026-10-28' (ISO) while every other surface says 'Wed 28 Oct'; goal results print the stored status word in lower case. Overdue reminders are not marked as overdue in results.
evidence: eval of the search listbox for 'reminder 2' → 'Reminder 2Due 2026-10-28'; shots/shell/search-iphone-q.png (Goal 2 · completed); js/core/search.js:113 ("Due " + r.due), :196 (sub: g.status)
fix: Format with the shared date helper used by Reminders ('Wed 28 Oct', 'Overdue · 28 Oct'), and map goal status to 'Reached'/'In progress'/'Missed'.
rootCause: search.js builds its own sub-lines instead of the owners' formatters.

title: Header controls on Graphite: the Assistant emblem is near-invisible and the four header controls are four different heights
detail: On the default dark theme the Assistant trigger's emblem (whispering-bloom-emblem-production.png, a dark mark with a little red) sits on a dark 38px circle and reads as a smudge; on Dawn it is fine. Header controls are 40px (review chip), 38px (bell, Assistant), 32px (sync dot) and 34px brand at 1470px, so their centres and outlines don't line up; on iPhone the review chip is 44x40 beside 44x44 buttons (below the 44px coarse target).
evidence: shots/shell/hdr-mac-right-crop.png (dark), shots/shell/dawn-bell-mac.png (Dawn); eval: chip 203x40, bell 38x38, assistant 38x38, syncdot 32x32 (mac); phone chip 44x40; index.html assistant-trigger img
fix: Use a light/outlined variant of the emblem (or the bloom brand mark) on dark themes, or tint via a mask with --text; size every header control from one token (--icon-btn, 44 on coarse) and give the chip min-block-size var(--hit-coarse) on touch.
rootCause: Raster emblem has no dark-theme variant; header controls size themselves from different tokens.

title: Review chip menu never names the review on iPhone ('Open · ready' / 'Skip review'), and Skip has no undo
detail: On the phone the chip is just the 夜 glyph; tapping it opens a menu whose items are 'Open — ready' and 'Skip review — nothing else changes', with no heading, so the user is not told it is the Evening review (or that 夜 means evening). The 'ready' hint repeats the chip state instead of saying what opening does. On the Mac opening a review is two steps when the chip could open it in one. 'Skip review' finishes the slot immediately (V().finish(slot,'skipped')) with no toast/Undo.
evidence: shots/shell/reviewchip-iphone.png, shots/shell/reviewchip-mac.png; js/modules/dayreview.js:705-709
fix: Give the menu a heading row ('Evening review · 3 steps') or make the first item 'Open the evening review'; make the hint describe the action; after Skip show a toast with Undo. Consider primary click = open, ▾ = Skip.
rootCause: Menu items assume the chip's text label is visible, which the phone header drops.

title: KOS.rerender() throws the page back to the top on every device: it saves/restores #main.scrollTop but #stage is the scroller
detail: Every non-navigation redraw (cloud pull, routine auto-tick, achievements touch, Google/Todoist cycle, a goal or money tick, the day review, and 144 KOS.rerender() call sites in 30 files, many after an in-page action) resets the scroll position. Reproduced at 1470x832: #/home scrolled to 600 → KOS.rerender() → 0; #/reminders scrolled to 900 → KOS.rerender() → 0. Browser Back to a long page also lands at the top (reminders 900 → Home → Back → 0). This contradicts the router contract ('a background pull that repaints the page you are on leaves … your scroll position exactly as they were', router.js:25-29, invariant 65) and the standing 'lost position on redraw' rule. Same on iPhone (402x874: #/home 800 → 0, #stage is the scroller there too).
evidence: eval: {'#/home': ['stage', 600, 0]}; eval reminders {b:[900,0], afterRerender:0, after Back: 0}; scroller probe: #stage overflow-y auto (scrollHeight 2152 / client 772), #main overflow visible; js/core/ui.js:353-356 (var top = main.scrollTop … main.scrollTop = top), js/core/ui.js:1521-1523 (main.innerHTML = ''; main.scrollTop = 0); iPhone eval ['stage',800,0]
fix: Introduce one KOS.ui.scrollRoot() (the #stage on wide layouts, document.scrollingElement on the phone) and use it in rerender (save before, restore after the view drew, and again on the next frame for async content) and in show() (reset to 0 on a real navigation; restore a remembered position per history index on Back/Forward, like the router already keeps args per index). Add a smoke test.
rootCause: The scroll container moved from #main to #stage (layout) but ui.js still saves/restores #main.scrollTop, which is always 0.

title: Navigating to the page you are already on pushes a duplicate history entry, so Back appears to do nothing
detail: KOS.show() always calls pushEntry() unless it is a _nav redraw; it never compares the new route with lastRendered. Clicking the rail item of the current section, the brand mark on Home, a subject pill for the open subject or a search result for the page in view each add an identical entry. Reproduced: on #/home, rail 'Home' + brand mark raised router depth 7 -> 9 and history.back() stayed on #/home; KOS.show('calendar') twice raised depth 3 -> 5 and history.back() left the user on #/calendar. On the installed app (no browser chrome) this makes Back/Alt+Left look broken.
evidence: eval: {d0:2,d1:3,d2:5,h1:'#/calendar'} and {d0:7,d1:9,hash:'#/home'}; js/core/router.js:226-238 (pushEntry when !opts._nav, no route===lastRendered check)
fix: In the KOS.show wrapper: if (!opts._nav && route === lastRendered) replaceEntry(route,arg) instead of pushEntry (still render, so a rail click on the current page refreshes/scrolls to top).
rootCause: The router wrapper treats every non-redraw show as a new navigation even when the route is unchanged.

title: The installed app has no Back control at all: the header's ‹ › were removed and iOS Home Screen apps have no browser Back
detail: index.html dropped #nav-back/#nav-fwd in 8fa52cb ('Back and Forward are the browser's own, plus Alt+Left/Right and the OS gestures in an installed app'). The manifest is display: standalone, and an iPad/iPhone Home Screen web app has no toolbar Back and no reliable edge-swipe Back, so the user's primary device (the installed iPad app) can only move by the rail or a page's own breadcrumb. Cross-links have no way home: open a goal, report week, exam or topic from Home, Search, the bell or a Calendar chip and there is no route back to where you were except re-finding it. main.js, ui.js:330 and router.js:212 still look up #nav-back/#nav-fwd (dead code). Help's 'Back / Forward' entry still promises arrows.
evidence: shots/shell/standalone-goal-ipad.png (header: brand, search, clock, review chip, bell, avatar; no Back); eval: document.getElementById('nav-back') === null; git show 8fa52cb -- index.html; manifest.webmanifest display:standalone; js/main.js:16-19, js/core/router.js:211-216
fix: Show a Back button in the header only when running standalone (matchMedia('(display-mode: standalone)') or navigator.standalone) or at phone width, enabled by KOS.canBack(); keep the browser's own Back elsewhere. Remove the dead lookups otherwise.
rootCause: The header arrows were removed for the browser case without a replacement for the standalone (installed) case.
devices: iPad installed app (primary), iPhone installed app

title: ui.js still keeps a second, dead navigation stack (navHist/navFwd, KOS.back/forward/canBack) that the router overwrites
detail: js/core/ui.js:325-336 and :409-420 define navHist/navFwd, KOS.back/forward/canBack/canForward and updateNavBtns, and KOS.show pushes to navHist on every navigation (:1556-1562). router.js then replaces KOS.back/forward/canBack/canForward with the history-based versions. The ui.js stack is still mutated on every show, and updateNavBtns/router.updateArrows both look up #nav-back/#nav-fwd, which no longer exist. The router's own header explains that two stacks that can disagree is how the arrows 'started lying'; keeping the dead one invites a future caller to read it.
evidence: js/core/ui.js:325-336, :409-420, :1556-1562; js/core/router.js:248-251; document.getElementById('nav-back') === null
fix: Delete navHist/navFwd and the ui.js back/forward functions; keep navCur only for the redraw key.
rootCause: The router was layered over ui.js's original stack without removing it.

title: Enter on a focused Cancel button CONFIRMS a non-danger confirm dialog (End session, Turn off notifications, Disconnect GitHub, Add a copy/Open existing...)
detail: KOS.ui.confirm adds a document keydown listener that calls close(true) on any Enter when !opts.danger, without looking at the event target. Keydown fires before the focused button's click, so Tab to Cancel (or 'Stay', 'Add a copy') and pressing Enter runs the affirmative action. Reproduced: confirm({title:'Replace?'}) -> focus Cancel -> Enter -> onYes ran. Affected non-danger confirms include Focus 'End early?' (ends and pays the session), 'Turn off closed-app notifications?', 'Disconnect the GitHub App?', 'Reset every permission?', 'Free up space', 'Keep in my cloud', 'Back to the defaults?' (FSRS), the sample/empty account switch, Japanese 'Leave the session?', the vault 'Already in the vault' (Enter on 'Add a copy' opens the existing entry instead) and the service-worker 'Update ready'. Keyboard and switch users on the Mac and iPad keyboard are affected.
evidence: eval: {enterOnCancel:'YES'}; js/core/ui.js:291-292 (function onKey(e){ if (e.key==='Enter' && !opts.danger) close(true); } on document); 51 ui.confirm call sites, the non-danger ones listed by grep in js/modules/focus.js, notifications.js, code.js, cardstats.js, governor-ui.js:450, jarun.js, medview.js, pwa.js:53
fix: Only treat Enter as yes when the target is not a button/link (e.g. if (e.key==='Enter' && !opts.danger && !(e.target.closest && e.target.closest('button,a,[role=button]'))) close(true)); or drop the document listener and rely on the focused confirm button's native Enter.
rootCause: The affirmative Enter shortcut is bound at document level and ignores which control has focus.

title: A dialog survives navigation: Back (or a rail/route change) leaves the confirm open over the new page, still bound to the old page's record
detail: KOS.show closes an open menu (closeOpenMenu) but not dialogs. Reproduced: on #/calendar open a danger confirm, press browser Back / swipe: the route changes to #/home behind the scrim and the 'Delete event?' dialog stays on top; confirming would delete a record of a page no longer on screen. The same with Alt+Left, a notification click (kos-open from the service worker routes through KOS.show) or the router's popstate. An editor dialog left open over another page saves into a page that is not shown.
evidence: eval: {dialogStillOpenAfterBack:true, hash:'#/home'}; js/core/ui.js:1566-1571 (closeOpenMenu only); js/core/router.js:284-300 (onPop renders without consulting the dialog stack)
fix: In onPop: if KOS.ui.topDialog() exists, close the top dialog instead of navigating (push the entry back with history.go(1) or pushState) - the mobile pattern 'Back closes the sheet'; in KOS.show for non-_nav navigations close every dialog in dialogStack (calling each overlay.close so editors can ask about unsaved changes).
rootCause: Dialogs are body-level overlays with no link to the route; navigation code only knows about menus.

title: Opening the bell puts focus on 'Mark all as read': one Enter/Space after opening clears every unread notice on every device, with no undo
detail: The bell popover's first focusable is the '✓ Mark all as read' link, and the shared menu focuses the first control on open. Keyboard: Tab to the bell, Enter (open), Enter again = 42 notices marked read (synced), the popover closes, and nothing offers Undo. Reading state drives other surfaces (Home's report card stays 'New' until its notification is read, invariant 102c), so this also silently retires the 'New' report. The page version (#/notifications) has the same unguarded button.
evidence: eval mac: bell focusOnOpen 'BUTTON:✓ Mark all as read'; js/modules/notifications.js:77-78 (markAllRead(); close()) and :140; KOS.notify.markAllRead has no undo path
fix: Focus the first notification row (or the panel heading) on open and put Mark all as read last; after marking, show a toast with Undo that restores the previous read map (the ids are known).
rootCause: Menu default focus = first focusable, and the bulk action is rendered first.

title: First run writes four fake 'SAMPLE — … (edit me)' events into the real calendar; the mock exam becomes a real assessment that drives Home, alerts and the bell
detail: On an empty account main.js calls KOS.calendar.seedSamples(), which addEvent()s a SAMPLE mock exam (alerts 7 days and 1 day), a coursework deadline, a study block and a weekly maths lesson. The mock is then migrated into the Exams hub as a real assessment (state.exams.assessments = ['SAMPLE — Mock exam (edit me)']), so on day one Home's Focus card says 'Revise for SAMPLE — Mock exam (edit me)', the daily goal reads 'Revise for: SAMPLE…', a toast and a bell notice fire ('⏰ SAMPLE — Mock exam (edit me) — 5 days away'), Upcoming lists both, and with Google Calendar connected they would be pushed two-way to the user's primary calendar. They are ordinary records: nothing marks them as samples or removes them, and the weekly lesson recurs forever. There is also no first-run welcome: the bell's other first notices are 'Afternoon review' and '23 plan topics carried over into this week' (the plan seed), and the Week's plan says '23 behind' on the first open. The app already has a proper separate Sample mode (KOS.dataMode 'sample').
evidence: shots/shell/empty-first-iphone.png, shots/shell/empty-home-mac.png; eval on reset account: assess ['SAMPLE — Mock exam (edit me)'], notify ['Afternoon review','SAMPLE — Mock exam (edit me)','23 plan topics carried over into this week'], toast text; js/modules/calendar.js:698-712; js/main.js:102
fix: Drop seedSamples (the Sample data mode covers demos) or mark seeded rows {sample:true} so the exam migration, alerts, notify, Home ladder and ext sync skip them, with one 'Remove the examples' action. Add a short first-run card on Home (connect cloud, pick subjects, import Collection) instead.
rootCause: A pre-hub demo seed still writes real records, and later domains (Exams migration, notifications, Google sync) treat them as the user's own.

title: Toast 'Undo' is unreachable without a pointer: the button is tabindex=-1 inside the aria-hidden #toast, and the spoken message never says Undo exists
detail: KOS.ui.toast(msg, bad, {label:'Undo', run}) appends the action button with tabindex '-1' into #toast, which carries aria-hidden='true'; the live region announces only msg. So keyboard users (Mac, iPad keyboard) cannot reach Undo, VoiceOver users never learn it exists, and there is no global ⌘Z outside the ink engine. The action toasts are the only Undo for: Home's plan tick (hub.js:964), Reminders' plan tick (reminders.js:344), the Daily Review's triage Tomorrow/Done/study block (dayreview.js:534,615,621,622). It also disappears after 8 s regardless of focus/hover (WCAG 2.2.1 timing).
evidence: eval: {ariaHidden:'true', tabindex:'-1', hitIsBtn:true}; js/core/ui.js:73-87; 6 call sites with {label:'Undo'}
fix: Give action toasts their own non-hidden container (role=status) with a focusable button; announce 'msg. Undo available, press ⌘Z' and bind ⌘Z/Ctrl+Z (outside text fields) to the most recent toast action while it is shown; pause the timer while hovered/focused.
rootCause: The toast was made aria-hidden for the live-region split (Phase F) before toasts gained actions.
devices: MacBook, iPad with keyboard, VoiceOver everywhere

title: 'Skip to content' navigates to Home instead of skipping: href='#main' is read by the hash router as an unknown route
detail: The skip link (the first Tab stop on every page) is <a href="#main">. Activating it changes location.hash to '#main'; router.js's hashchange listener parses it, finds no such route and calls home(), so from #/calendar the keyboard user lands on #/home with a new history entry replaced. The one bypass mechanism for keyboard and switch users (WCAG 2.4.1) throws them off the page they were on.
evidence: eval mac: {before:'#/calendar', after:'#/home', active:'main'}; index.html:61; js/core/router.js:302-306 (hashchange -> onPop -> parse fails -> home())
fix: Give the link a click handler that preventDefault()s and calls document.getElementById('main').focus({preventScroll:false}) (or make router.parse ignore hashes that do not start with '#/').
rootCause: An in-page fragment link in an app that uses the fragment for routing.

title: On iPhone, Money's six views and Goals' This week/This month/All/Done tabs are unreachable: the phone hides the page tabs and its ▾ sheet lists the section's pages instead
detail: Money (Overview, Transactions, Budgets, Recurring, Pots, Month and year) and Goals (This week, This month, All, Done) mark their workspace tabs data-phone-tabs. At ≤700px components.css hides every [data-phone-tabs] because the phone title bar's ▾ is meant to offer them, but mobile-shell's destinations() only falls back to the page's tabs when the section has NO subnav. Productivity has a subnav (Focus, Reminders, Routines, Calendar, Money, Goals), so the ▾ sheet on Money lists Productivity's pages and the Money tabs are offered nowhere. Measured at 402px: all six Money tabs and all four Goals tabs have width 0, the sheet shows Focus Timer…Goals, and Money's Overview has no link to Transactions/Recurring/Pots/Month. Money's 'Add entry', Transactions list, recurring bills and pots can only be reached by typing a URL. Achievements and the Governor (no subnav) work because the fallback applies there.
evidence: shots/shell/money-iphonesafari.png, shots/shell/money-sheet-iphonesafari.png, shots/shell/money-overview-iphone.png; eval: #/money tabs visible 0 of 6, subnavItems 6; #/goals visible 0 of 4; css/components.css:654 (#main[data-phone-title] [data-phone-tabs] {display:none}); js/modules/mobile-shell.js:457-468 (destinations: subnav first, page tabs only when no subnav); js/modules/money.js:128, js/modules/goals.js:303
fix: When the page carries [data-phone-tabs] and a subnav exists, show both in the sheet (section pages, then the page's own views under a sub-heading) or keep the page's tabs visible as a scroller under the title bar; add a smoke assertion that every [role=tab] in #main is visible or offered by the sheet at 402px.
rootCause: The phone title bar treats 'section strip' and 'page tabs' as alternatives, but Money and Goals have both; the CSS hides the tabs unconditionally.
devices: iPhone (and any width ≤700, incl. iPad Slide Over)

title: Search ranks specification hits in syllabus order, not by relevance: 'binary' shows 'Fields, records and files' first and cuts 'Unsigned binary', 'Two's complement' and Code's 'Binary search trees' past the six shown
detail: The Specification domain takes KOS.hub.search's first six results without ranking: the hits come in SEARCH_INDEX order (CS 4.1… then Maths then Code), and search.js's rank() (title-starts-with first) is applied to every other domain but not to spec. For 'binary' 30 leaves match; title matches sit at positions 1,3,4,7,8,12,14,15 so 'Unsigned binary and binary arithmetic' (7), 'Signed binary using two's complement' (8) and all of Code's never appear, while 'Fields, records and files' (body text 'binary file') is first. 'integration' lists 'Partial fractions' above 'Integration as limit of a sum'; 'dijkstra' lists 'Kinds of abstraction' and 'Reverse Polish notation' (flashcard matches). There is no 'show all results' row, so a result past six cannot be reached.
evidence: eval: search('binary') title hits at indexes [1,3,4,7,8,12,14,15] of 30; listbox options for 'binary','integration','dijkstra' (printed); js/core/search.js:31 (PER_DOMAIN 6), :42-49 (rank), :60-73 (specDomain: res.slice(0, PER_DOMAIN), no rank); js/modules/hub.js searchSpec (returns specHits in index order)
fix: Score spec hits: exact title > title word-start > title contains > spec text > flashcard, then subject order; rank before slicing; add a final 'See all N results' option that opens a results page (or expands the domain).
rootCause: Spec search is a filter, not a ranker, and the cross-domain layer truncates before ranking.

title: docs/GUIDE.md (the plain-words guide) stops at 26 Oct: Creatives and Mind are listed as 'still on the way', and Achievements, Connections, the art/shop release and the Stage are absent
detail: GUIDE.md was last changed 26 Oct 2026. Since then Mind (29 Oct), Creatives (30 Oct), Google Calendar/Tasks/Todoist (30 Oct), Achievements and the Badge Wall (31 Oct) and the art and shop release (1 Nov) shipped. §5 'What is still on the way' still lists 'A Creatives study space…and Mind' and 'new things for the gold shop — such as outfits for Kurenai' as future. Counts: Achievement/Badge 0, Connections/Todoist 0, Wardrobe 0, Pencil 0, Creatives 1 (only in §5), FSRS 1; there is no Mind or Creatives tour section (§2 has Code and Japanese only), no Exams & Deadlines hub section (Exams: 3 passing mentions), no Routines/Daily Review section beyond one line. Money (6) and Goals (4) are covered in a paragraph each, so the in-app Help (which has none) and GUIDE.md disagree on what exists.
evidence: docs/GUIDE.md headings (lines 45-418), :418-430; git log -1 docs/GUIDE.md = 26 Oct 2026; grep -ci counts
fix: Add tour sections for Mind, Creatives, the Exams hub, Routines and the Daily Review, Achievements, the Stage and shop, Connections; move shipped items out of §5. Generate Help's sections and GUIDE.md from one source (or have a smoke test that every rail destination is named in both).
rootCause: Two hand-kept guides with no release checklist item or test.

title: iPad-portrait overlay rail: Escape does not close it, a tap on the page both closes it and activates what was under the finger, and its open state is persisted
detail: At 701-1080px the opened rail floats over the page. Escape leaves it open (s1 'full' -> after Escape 'full'); focus stays on the toggle rather than entering the rail. The only dismissals are a destination or a pointerdown on #stage, and that pointerdown does not cancel the tap, so tapping the page to dismiss also presses whatever control was under the finger (tap-through). ui.railOpenNarrow is saved, so an overlay left open comes back open over the page on the next launch of the installed app.
evidence: eval at 820x1180: {s1:'full', focusIn:false, afterEsc:'full'}; js/main.js:71-81 (no Escape handler; stage pointerdown closes without preventing the click); :63-69 (setRail persists railOpenNarrow)
fix: Treat the narrow overlay like the spine drawer: add a scrim (or capture the first pointerdown and preventDefault/stopPropagation the following click), close on Escape (unless a dialog is open) and return focus to the toggle; don't persist the narrow overlay state (start closed).
rootCause: The narrow rail reuses the persistent open/closed preference of the docked rail instead of being a transient drawer.

title: Tapping a notification often lands on a generic page: Daily Review notices open Routines (not the review), routine-window notices ignore the routine, goal notices open the Goals list, and cold-start pushes drop object args
detail: KOS.notify.open(item) does KOS.show(item.view, item.arg). Daily Review items carry {view:'routines', arg:{review:'afternoon'}} and routine windows {arg:{routine:id}}, but KOS.views.routines only reads arg.edit or a tab string, so both open Routines › Today and the review sheet never opens (verified: shots/shell/notify-review-open.png, no review dialog). Goal notices ('Goal reached — Goal 5') are pushed with {view:'goals', arg:null} and open the list (#/goals) instead of #/goals/<id>. The service worker builds its own cold-start hash ('#/'+view+'/'+arg, objects dropped, sw.js:147) instead of the router's routeFor, so a closed-app push for a review, a topic or a report week opens the section landing. One connected OS should take a notice straight to its record.
evidence: shots/shell/notify-review-open.png; eval: notify kinds review:routines:object, goal:goals:null; goal open -> '#/goals'; js/core/notify.js:196-199; js/core/dayreview.js:713; js/core/routines.js:560; js/modules/routines.js:469-473; js/core/goals.js:807; sw.js:147,154
fix: Routines view: if arg.review open KOS.reviewSheet for that slot; if arg.routine open the player/editor. Goals notices: link {view:'goals', arg:{id}}. In the push payload send the router hash (KOS.router.routeFor) and let sw.js open it verbatim; for in-app kos-open keep view+arg.
rootCause: Producers set view/arg shapes the target views never learned to read, and the SW re-implements routing.

title: iPad touch targets in the shell: the rail toggle is 24x24 and the collapsed rail buttons are 30px wide (narrower than their own 32px tile)
detail: At iPad portrait (820x1180, pointer coarse, no hover) the collapsed rail is the default and the only way to expand it is the round toggle on the rail edge, measured 24x24 CSS px (layout.css keeps it at --hit-dense on purpose, citing invariant 69, but that exception is written for dense calendar chips, not the primary navigation control). The seven rail destinations measure 30x44: the button is narrower than the 32px kanji tile it contains (button min-inline-size:0 with padding 4px 0), so the hit area is smaller than what is drawn. The review chip in the header is 40px tall (under the 44px touch minimum).
evidence: eval --size ipad: rail-toggle rect {x:59,y:76,w:24,h:24}; rail items [BUTTON,x21,w30,h44,padding 4px 0]; review chip 203x40; shots/shell/rail-tiles-ipad-crop.png; css/layout.css:213-235 (.k-rail-toggle 24px, coarse override to --hit-dense), :297-309 and :375 (tile 32px, item padding 4px 0)
fix: On coarse pointers give the rail toggle a 44px invisible hit area (a ::after inset that does not overlap the spine) or make it a 44px circle; give collapsed .k-rail-item min-inline-size: 44px (the rail is 71px wide); raise the header chip to the 44px touch height used by the other header controls.
devices: iPad portrait (and iPad landscape for the toggle)
rootCause: The dense-size exception was applied to the rail toggle to avoid an oval; the compact rail item has no minimum width.

title: A hidden live region announces a bare number ("545") at boot: #node-count is aria-live but only holds the total leaf count
detail: index.html keeps <span id=node-count class=sr-only aria-live=polite>; refreshRailCounters writes the total number of specification leaves into it. A screen reader therefore says "545" (no words) shortly after the app loads, and again whenever the total changes (a curriculum release). Nothing else reads the element.
evidence: eval mac: live regions [search-count:"", node-count:"545", kos-live-polite:"Routines", kos-live-assertive:""]; index.html:119; js/modules/hub.js:319-321
fix: Drop aria-live from #node-count (or delete the element: no reader uses it); invariant 66 already makes KOS.a11y.announce the sole live-region route.
rootCause: Leftover live region from the pre-Graphite rail that showed a node count; violates invariant 66 (announce is the sole live-region route).

title: Hold-⌘ shortcut sheet is a fixed list: it shows Ink/PDF/Flashcard keys on every page and omits the shortcuts that exist (Backspace back, Esc, Money row keys, the Daily Review and routine player arrows and S, the story keys, the quiz arrow)
detail: Holding ⌘ on Home (no ink, no PDF, no cards on screen) shows the same four groups: Anywhere (/ and ⌥← ⌥→), Ink, A PDF, Flashcards. The app has more shortcuts than these and none is listed: Backspace = Back (main.js), Esc closes dialogs/menus/drawer, Money rows (Space ticks, E edits; money.js:607-609) and the month strip arrows (money.js:361), the Daily Review steps ← → (dayreview.js:181-182), the routine player ← → and S to skip (routineplayer.js:57-59), the report story ← → Space (reportstory.js:627-629), the quiz → for next (quiz.js:144). The key column is not aligned ("Page Up / Down" pushes its label to x=409 while the others start at x=404) and the kbd glyphs render at ~10px mono, smaller than the label text.
evidence: shots/shell/cmd-hold-mac.png; sheet rect {x:275,y:112,w:920,h:237}; js/core/desk.js:39-44 (static SHORTCUTS array)
fix: Build the sheet from a registry: global keys plus a group contributed by the current view (KOS.desk.register(viewId, rows)); show only groups relevant to the page; align keys in a fixed-width column (grid) and use the 12-13px kbd token.
rootCause: SHORTCUTS is a hard-coded array in desk.js written for the iPad ink release; later features added keys without a place to declare them.

title: Kurenai cannot open 13 current pages: app_navigate's view list stops before Money, Reports, Routines, Files, Achievements, Connections, Storage, Pen and ink, the Assistant and the four study spaces (Code, Japanese, Mind, Creatives)
detail: The Assistant's navigation tool takes view from a fixed enum NAV_VIEWS, and subject/ref take subject from SUBJECTS = [compsci, maths, it]. Every view registered since mid-October is missing: pen, code, japanese, creatives, mind, routines, files, storage, connections, assistant, money, reports, achievements. Asking "open Money" or "take me to my week in review" or "open Japanese lesson 1.2" cannot be done by the tool (the model either refuses or picks a wrong view); a Code/Japanese/Mind/Creatives lesson ref cannot be opened at all. The tool list in the system prompt therefore also tells the model these pages do not exist as destinations.
evidence: eval: Object.keys(KOS.views) minus NAV_VIEWS = [pen, code, japanese, creatives, mind, routines, files, storage, connections, assistant, money, reports, achievements]; js/core/aitools.js:2735-2740 (NAV_VIEWS), :30 (SUBJECTS), :2741-2766 (app_navigate)
fix: Derive NAV_VIEWS from KOS.views (minus internal ones) or from the router's route table, take subject from KOS.subjects.ids(), and accept the arg shapes the router accepts (e.g. money page, reports week). Add a smoke check that every registered view is navigable.
rootCause: Hand-maintained enum duplicated from the route table; nothing fails when a view is added.

title: KOS.show with an unknown view id draws a blank page and pushes it into history (#/archive, #/nonsense) instead of falling back like a typed URL does
detail: A typed or stale hash (#/nonsense) is replaced with Home, but a programmatic KOS.show("archive") or KOS.show("nonsense") empties #main, leaves no rail item current and pushes the bad route into history, so Back/Forward return to the blank page and a reload of that URL lands on Home. The renderer silently skips a missing view (ui.js try { if (KOS.views[viewId]) ... }) and the router wrapper pushes the route regardless.
evidence: shots/shell/archive-empty-mac.png (blank main at #/archive); eval {has:false, h3:"#/nonsense", mainLen:0}; js/core/ui.js:1592; js/core/router.js:226-238
fix: In KOS.show, if !KOS.views[viewId] log a console.warn and redirect to home with replace (same rule as router invalid routes) before pushing any entry.
rootCause: Unknown-route handling exists only in the hashchange/popstate path, not in KOS.show.

title: No first run: a new device opens straight onto a busy Home that is already "23 behind" with 3 unread notices, and nothing offers to sign in and bring the account's data over
detail: After a reset (a new iPad/iPhone, a cleared Safari, or the Home Screen app installed fresh) the app boots to Home with: the bell showing 3 unread ("SAMPLE — Mock exam (edit me)" alert, "23 plan topics carried over into this week", "Evening review"), Week's plan "23 behind", Upcoming listing a NEA milestone and two SAMPLE items, a Daily goal "Revise for: SAMPLE — Mock exam" and the review chip. There is no welcome, no step that explains what the app is, and no prompt to sign in to cloud sync, which is the only way the user's real data reaches the new device; the sign-in lives on Archive (#/data) with no link from Home, the bell or the empty states (the sync chip is hidden while signed out). A first open therefore shows alarming but fake state and buries the action that matters.
evidence: shots/shell/empty-home-mac.png, shots/shell/empty-first-iphone.png, shots/shell/empty-home-ipad.png; eval after reset: notify items [cal:1:2026-11-10:10080 SAMPLE — Mock exam, pace:carry:2026-11-02 23 plan topics carried over, review:evening:2026-11-05], #sync-status hidden; grep: no onboarding/firstRun code in js/; js/modules/calendar.js:704-708 (sample events); js/main.js:106 (KOS.pacing.ensureSeeded seeds the whole plan, past weeks included)
fix: Add a one-screen first run (shown while the state is pristine and signed out): "Sign in to bring your data" (cloud), "Start fresh", and the theme choice; suppress the sample calendar events and the pacing carry-over notice until the user chooses; show a quiet "Not synced — sign in" header chip while signed out on a device that has never synced.
devices: all (a new device or a fresh Home Screen install)
rootCause: Boot seeds sample events and the full plan unconditionally and has no pristine-state branch.

title: <body> also carries data-theme ("legacy hook, harmless"), so every derived token is re-derived on body: anything that sets the theme on <html> alone renders Graphite's derivations under Dawn's roles
detail: governor.js writes the theme to both html and body. tokens.css declares its derived tokens on ":root, [data-theme]", so body re-computes all of them from the inherited roles; themes.css' Dawn restatements win again only because body carries the same id. If the two ever differ (the QA harness sets html only; any future preview/try-on code that sets html, or a stale body value), the body-level Graphite derivations shadow Dawn's restated ones: measured with html=atelier-dawn, body="": Home hero kicker colour oklch(0.8 0.04 235) (unreadable, ~1.2:1 on the light hero) vs oklch(0.42 0.08 235) when both carry atelier-dawn; --home-hero-ink, --home-goal-ink, --home-hero-scrim, --bk-kicker-ink, --mx-wash, --gv-rec-bg and --shadow-ink all differ between html and body. NOTE FOR THE AUDIT: every screenshot taken with the harness' --theme flag has this mixed rendering, so Dawn contrast findings based on those shots should be re-checked with KOS.governor.setTheme.
evidence: shots/shell/empty-home-iphonesafari.png (harness --theme: faint date and Daily goal kickers); eval html vs body token comparison all false; eval after KOS.governor.setTheme(atelier-dawn): kickers oklch(0.42 0.08 235)/oklch(0.42 0.06 200); js/core/governor.js:777-778; css/tokens.css:1262 (:root, [data-theme]); css/themes.css:62; audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/kos.mjs:107-108
fix: Remove document.body.dataset.theme (nothing reads it as a hook; check with grep), or narrow tokens.css to ":root, [data-theme]:not(body)". Fix the harness to call KOS.governor.setTheme instead of setting the attribute.
rootCause: Duplicate theme attribute on body combined with a derived-token block that matches any [data-theme] element.

title: One toast slot: each new toast replaces the last, so in the Daily Review (or Home's Today ticks) only the most recent triage can be undone; toasts also vanish after a fixed 2.6 s whatever their length
detail: KOS.ui.toast writes into the single #toast node (t.textContent = msg) and restarts one timer. The Daily Review's triage buttons (Tomorrow, ✓ Done, Study block, the step actions) each show "<title> · marked done — Undo"; triaging three items in a row leaves only the third's Undo — the first two are committed with no way back, although invariant 144 promises Undo for every change a review makes. Same on Home's Today ticks and Reminders' plan ticks. Any unrelated toast in the 8 s window (a save, a Focus message, the achievements count) also wipes a pending Undo. Plain toasts last 2.6 s regardless of length: "You already had 44 badge tiers — they are on the Wall." or an error with its reason cannot be read in that time (and the toast cannot be paused by hover or focus).
evidence: js/core/ui.js:71-87 (single node, textContent replace, fixed 2600/8000 ms); Undo toasts at js/modules/dayreview.js:534, :615, :621, :622; js/modules/hub.js:964; js/modules/reminders.js:344
fix: Queue or stack toasts (at most 3, newest on top) and never drop one that carries an action until its time ends; scale duration to text length (e.g. 2.6 s + 60 ms/char, max 10 s) and pause on hover/focus; in the Daily Review keep an inline "Undo" on each triaged row instead of relying on the toast.
rootCause: The toast is a single-slot primitive and Undo was layered on it without a queue.

title: The URL does not record many pages: the Wall's tabs and set pages, an opened assignment or reminder, a review run all collapse to the bare route, so a reload, a bookmark or the Home Screen app relaunch lands on the wrong page
detail: router.js only has ENCODE/DECODE entries for ref, subject, governor, code, japanese, creatives, mind, sims, money, routines, exams, goals, assistant, help, reports and pacing. Views that take an argument without a codec get a URL without it: KOS.show("achievements","titles") writes #/achievements, and the documented deep links #/achievements/sets|recent|showcase|titles|set/<id> (CLAUDE.md ownership map) all open on Sets (cold load of #/achievements/sets even rewrites the hash to #/achievements). KOS.show("assignments",{id}) (from Files' Where it's linked), KOS.show("reminders",{id,section}) (from search), KOS.show("review",{tab,run}) (Cram from the Exams Companion, Due today's queue buttons) and cardstats likewise. In-session Back works (argMemo keeps the arg per entry) but a reload, an iPad Home Screen app that iOS relaunched, or a copied link loses the place. This is also why a push notification opened from a cold start drops its object argument (see the earlier notification finding).
evidence: eval: #/achievements/recent and #/achievements/titles render with the Sets tab selected; cold load of #/achievements/sets -> hash #/achievements; shots/shell/ach-titles-deeplink-mac.png (hash #/achievements/titles, Sets selected); js/core/router.js:30-148 (ENCODE/DECODE lack achievements, assignments, reminders, review, cardstats), :150-154 routeFor; js/modules/achievements.js:110-115 (reads arg as "tab/id"); js/core/files.js:146; js/core/search.js:115; js/modules/due.js:103-173
fix: Add codecs for achievements (tab, set/<id>), assignments (id), reminders (id/section), review (tab, run) and cardstats; better, make each view declare its own route codec next to its KOS.views registration and have a smoke test round-trip every KOS.show call site through routeFor/parse.
devices: all (worst in the installed iPad/iPhone app, which iOS relaunches)
rootCause: Route codecs live in a central table in router.js that new views/args were not added to; routeFor silently drops unknown args.

title: Reports has no rail item marked: on #/reports and every report page no destination is current (Reports lives under Home)
detail: On #/reports and #/reports/week/<start> the rail (and the phone tab bar) shows no current item, so the user loses their place in the hierarchy; CLAUDE.md places Reports under Home with no rail item of its own, and other rail-less pages (Achievements -> Governor, Notifications/Help/Files/Connections -> Archive) do mark their parent.
evidence: eval: {#/reports: cur:""}, {#/reports/week/2026-10-26: cur:""}; compare #/achievements cur "守Governor", #/connections cur "蔵Archive"
fix: Map the reports view to the Home rail item in the rail/tab-bar section table (wherever achievements->governor is mapped).
rootCause: Reports missing from the view-to-section map.

title: iPhone in landscape gets the iPad shell with nothing for its height or the Dynamic Island: the rail's profile chip is cut off below the screen and no left/right safe-area insets exist anywhere
detail: Turned sideways an iPhone 17 is 874x402 CSS px, above the 700px phone breakpoint, so it gets the tablet composition: 60px header, kanji rail, Home hero. The rail is 342px tall with 364px of content and overflow visible, so the profile chip (level/HP/gold, the way to the Governor) is drawn at y=382-420, past the 402px viewport and unreachable. index.html uses viewport-fit=cover but no CSS uses env(safe-area-inset-left/right), so in landscape the brand, the rail tiles and the left edge of every page sit under the Dynamic Island side of the screen (inset about 59px on iPhone 17).
evidence: shots/shell/iphone-landscape-home.png (874x402); eval {rail:[342,364,"visible"], profile:[382,420], vh:402}; grep env(safe-area-inset-left|right) in css/ = 0; index.html:5 viewport-fit=cover; css/layout.css:437-440 (only top/bottom insets, phone tier only)
fix: Pad #topbar and #cols with env(safe-area-inset-left/right); let #rail scroll (overflow-y:auto) or hide the profile chip when the rail is shorter than its content; consider treating a short landscape viewport (max-height ~500px) with the phone composition via a feature query on height rather than a new width breakpoint.
rootCause: Composition is chosen by width only; safe-area handling written for portrait phones.

title: Header sync status is an unlabelled 8px grey dot: signed out, offline and idle look identical, and on iPad/iPhone (no hover) nothing says what it is; the search box also shows a "/" key hint on touch devices
detail: #sync-status is a 32-44px button whose text is hidden (font-size:0, color transparent) and whose only visual is an 8px dot: teal synced, amber in flight, red error, and the same muted grey for Signed out, Offline and idle (data-sync=idle for all three). Its meaning lives in the title attribute (hover only) and the aria-label. On the seeded but signed-out account the user therefore sees a grey dot after the Assistant emblem that never explains that cloud sync is off. On the iPad portrait and landscape headers the search field still shows the "/" keyboard-shortcut badge although the device has no hover and usually no keyboard.
evidence: shots/shell/hdr-ipad-crop.png (grey dot at far right, "/" badge in the search box); shots/shell/hdr-right-mac-crop2.png; eval: sync-status outerHTML text "Signed out", data-sync=idle, title "Cloud sync — Signed out (click for details)"; js/modules/cloudui.js:68-85 (state map: anything but synced/syncing/pending/error -> idle); css/layout.css:148-153
fix: Give signed-out and offline their own look (a struck or hollow dot, or a short text chip "Not synced"/"Offline" at widths that allow it); show the state in words in the phone More sheet; hide the "/" badge under (hover: none).
rootCause: Status chip reduced to a dot in the Graphite redesign with the label moved into title only.
